page: The UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-384GB is a Cloud Native virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor. This configuration provides 64 vCPUs with a shared CPU allocation, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, which translates to 6.0 GB of memory per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile characterized by a trade-off between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is limited, with stress-ng single-core metrics in the bottom 10% and single-threaded compression tests in the bottom 25%. Conversely, multi-core execution is highly capable, with the Passmark CPU score, extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests all placing in the top 25%. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also performs in the top 25%. Memory performance is mixed; cached small-block read bandwidth is strong, while uncached large-block read and write speeds remain in the middle 50%.

Given its shared CPU architecture and high memory capacity, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for resource-dense, parallelized workloads rather than sustained single-core compute tasks. It is structurally suited for multi-threaded applications, database operations, static web serving, and moderate LLM prompt processing where parallel threads can offset the lower single-core clock speed.
